newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria's Sofia Municipal Bank gets full licence.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria's Sofia Municipal Bank gets full licence.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) granted a full banking licence to the Sofia Municipal Bank (SMB) for operations at home and abroad, a BNB official said on Friday.
"The central bank board decided to extend a full licence to the Sofia Municipal Bank after the required minimum capital was fully paid in," the official told Reuters.
Under Bulgaria's current banking regulations the minimum required capital for a full licence is 2.2 billion levs and for a domestic one 1.4 billion levs.
The SMB was licensed for domestic operations alone in March 1996.

The SMB's paid-in capital now amounted to 2.36 billion levs and was distributed among the Sofia Municipality and seventeen municipal companies, the bank's chief executive director Vania Vassileva said.

SMB's capital was raised to 2.36 billion levs from 805 million levs through a transfer of the 1996 net profit of 411 million levs into the share capital and a new share issue covering the remainder, Vasileva said.
The Sofia Municipality holds a majority stake of around 63 percent in the capital, Vasileva said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 911 88
